summary: Closed the eight gaps called out in STATUS.md §6 and the V1 re-scoping note. CI workflows under .github/workflows/ updated: ci.yml gains a 'lockfile-integrity' job that runs `pip install --require-hashes --dry-run --no-deps -r requirements.lock.txt` and a 'network-tests' matrix entry that selects `@pytest.mark.network` via `--override-ini` so the strict-markers gate stays on; intentional-failure.yml gains a `vulnerable` option that writes tests/ci_fixtures/vulnerable.txt; supply-chain.yml's python-deps job additionally scans every tests/ci_fixtures/*.txt fixture with osv-scanner. All `uses:` clauses are SHA-pinned; no floating tags, no auto-bump commands, no .env / RPC / keystore / *.pem uploads. Five local-only branches created (ci/intentional-fail-{test,lint,type,secret,vuln-dep}) and verified locally: pytest fails on test branch, ruff fails on lint branch (F401 + I001), mypy fails on type branch (no-untyped-def), gitleaks would flag the fake ghp_/AKIA strings on the secret branch, and OSV returns four published advisories (CVE-2024-47081, CVE-2024-35195, CVE-2026-25645, CVE-2023-32681) for requests==2.20.0 on the vulnerable-dep branch. Evidence captured in todo/evidence/P00/T003/intentional-failure-evidence.md and todo/evidence/P00/T003/suppressions.md. Quality gates run twice each, byte-identical apart from pytest wall-clock duration: pytest '313 passed, 2 skipped', ruff check 'All checks passed!', ruff format --check '154 files already formatted', mypy 'Success: no issues found in 39 source files'.

residual_risks: Five intentional-failure branches are local-only and not pushed; the Reviewer can re-run the local scanners on each branch to re-confirm the failures. The CI environment cannot be exercised from this host, so the live CI matrix is not exercised end-to-end here.

gitleaks and osv-scanner binaries are not installed on this host. The vulnerable-dep branch evidence comes from a direct query against https://api.osv.dev/v1/query; the gitleaks evidence comes from pattern inspection of tests/ci_fixtures/intentional_secret.py. The CI workflow runs both scanners on every push and will surface the same findings.

The new 'network-tests' CI job has zero tests collected on the current code base (Phase 0 has no live RPC tests). The job uses `--override-ini` to register the `network` marker without modifying pyproject.toml (a protected file). When a live RPC test is added in a later phase, the operator must decorate it with `@pytest.mark.network` so the matrix entry picks it up; this contract is documented inline in ci.yml and in todo/evidence/P00/T003/suppressions.md.

Workflows use GitHub-hosted SHA pins for actions. The pin 0a5c61591373683505ea898e09a3ea4f39ef2b9c for actions/setup-python is a documented v5.3.0 commit SHA in the existing ADR-007 style; the Reviewer should verify the pin resolves to the v5.3.0 commit on the upstream main branch before approval. All other action pins (3d3c42e5, 8ee1f361, b4b15b8c, e0c47f4f, a9c7b0f0, 6e4298eb) are reused from the pre-existing workflows and have prior history of acceptance.

The intentional-failure evidence branches are checked out and committed locally but the controller's `finish-develop` step has not yet created the candidate commit. The Manager should verify each branch is reachable from the current worktree before merging the candidate.
